newsitem.title: USA: Signet seeks corporate trust business buyer.
newsitem.headline: Signet seeks corporate trust business buyer.

text.p: Signet Banking Corp said on Wednesday it seeks a buyer for its corporate trust business, incuding bond trustee and paying agent services for corporate and municipal customers.
Signet said it is contacting potential buyers and hopes to complete the sale by the fourth quarter of 1997.

The company said the decision to get out of the corporate trust business was not related to its current business redesign, which is intended to accelerate Signet's transformation from a regional bank to a national, information-based financial company.

"Our corporate trust business, while profitable, is a scale-driven business that would require a tremendous investment to remain competitive in a consolidating industry ...," Signet Chairman Malcolm McDonald said in a statement.

Signet will continue to offer escrow services for its corporate clients, and other trust services it offers will not be affected by the sell-off of the corporate trust book of business, the company said.
Signet has offices in Virginia, Maryland and the District of Columbia. It reported net income of $124.9 million, or $2.06 per share, for 1996.
